name: VA-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Walkinshaw with huge financial advantage ($2.8M raised, $979K on hand)
Republican Purves essentially unfunded ($10,780 raised, $200 cash)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Walkinshaw holds a D+18 seat as an incumbent with a massive fundraising edge, while Purves has raised barely ten thousand dollars and has no outside support. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Democratic hold, so the forecast stays near the baseline.
model.watch: Any late surge in Republican outside spending or an unexpected polling shift could narrow the margin, though a flip remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Virginia's 11th District leans heavily Democratic, and first-term incumbent James Walkinshaw is running for a full term with the advantages that come with incumbency. He has raised about $2.8 million and holds nearly $1 million on hand, supplemented by substantial outside support. Republican Arthur Purves has raised roughly $10,000 with almost no cash remaining, and no outside groups are active on his behalf. A Green Party candidate is also on the ballot but is not a significant factor.

With no public polling in the race, the picture rests on the district's strong partisan lean, the lopsided money gap, and prediction markets that price a Democratic win at about 97 percent. Everything points to a safe Democratic hold, with the only real question being the size of the margin.
